thread:
Maya (Design): dropped a new mock for the inference throughput chart. feedback specifically wanted on axis scaling (linear vs log), how we call out spikes, and legend density. link: https://redwood.design/figma/throughput-v2

deploy-bot: preview image generated for file throughput-v2 (v5)

Noah (Eng): nice! first thought: raw throughput ranges 10 r/s to 40k r/s. linear scale squashes small values; log might make trends clearer but confuses non-technical users

Priya (Product): log can be surprising. If we use log, we should annotate the axis with a label like "log scale" and maybe a tooltip explaining why. Non-expert users keep asking "why did it jump down?"

Liam (Data Viz): agree with annotation. Another option: use dual-axis or small-multiples: primary linear chart for main baseline, and a mini log inset for seeing orders-of-magnitude spikes

Ravi (Accessibility): a11y: whatever you do, the axis label needs to be programmatically discoverable. If you use an inset or dual view, ensure screen readers can reach both and understand the relationship

Maya (Design): hmm, inset could be cool but might clutter. For spikes, I mocked a small badge above the chart: "5 spikes > 10k r/s". Thoughts on copy?

Priya (Product): short/catchy is good. maybe "5 bursts > 10k r/s" — "bursts" maps better to throughput context

Noah (Eng): implementation note: marking every spike client-side is costly. We'll compute spike summaries server-side (percentile-based) and send a compact list of spike buckets to render badges

Liam (Data Viz): badge approach wins for glanceability. Also add a nuance: differentiate sustained high periods vs single-sample spikes. badge copy could be "3 sustained, 2 single-sample" but that's wordy. Alternative: icons: flame for sustained, dot for single-sample

Ravi (Accessibility): icons need alt text. For example: "3 sustained bursts above 10k requests per second". Also ensure badges are keyboard focusable and announced by SR when focused

Maya (Design): notes on legend: when there are just 1-2 series, inline top-left looks clean. For 4+ series, we should collapse into an expandable legend with search. Any layout constraints from eng?

Noah (Eng): expandable legend ok. For perf, we prefer canvas for the main line rendering and an HTML legend overlay for interactions. Canvas + DOM mix is our current pattern and scales best for many points

Liam (Data Viz): about units: consider auto-SI formatting (k, M) for throughput. But avoid switching unit mid-chart; show axis ticks with units like "Requests/s (k)" if we scale values by 1k internally

Priya (Product): product preference: add a small unit dropdown: auto / raw / per-minute. Some customers compare per-second vs per-minute; helpful for exports/screenshots

Maya (Design): smoothing: some stakeholders want a moving average for clarity, others said it masks regressions. propose default OFF, and a small toggle that when ON shows the smoothing window (e.g., MA(1m)). Also display a faint raw line beneath the smoothed curve

Noah (Eng): technically doable. For server-side aggregation we can precompute moving averages at a few windows (30s, 1m, 5m) to avoid heavy client CPU. We'll send both raw-sampled tiles and precomputed smoothed tiles

Liam (Data Viz): outlier handling: options are: a) axis break, b) capped axis + badge, c) annotate points with "outlier" marker. I still think c) + badge summary is least surprising. If you cap axis, visually indicate with a small chevron on the top tick

Ravi (Accessibility): +1 for explicit annotations. If you use chevrons or broken axes, include descriptive aria-labels like "axis capped at 50k r/s; 4 values above cap"

Maya (Design): copy decision: axis label should be explicit: "Throughput (requests/s)" and ticks use unit suffixes like "10k". Subtitle under title will show active unit and smoothing: e.g., "Unit: auto • Smoothing: off"

Priya (Product): export/PNG should include the subtitle so screenshots don't lose context. Also include a small legend key showing applied transforms (downsampling, smoothing)

Noah (Eng): regarding downsampling: we'll use LTTB (largest triangle three buckets) for client-friendly downsampling, and keep an outlier index separate so spikes aren't lost. For zoom we fetch raw tiles

Liam (Data Viz): color palette: pick a set of 8 that are color-blind friendly and meet contrast. Also add pattern overlays (dashed/dotted) as a fallback for print/greyscale

Ravi (Accessibility): I'll publish a short checklist: contrast ratios, keyboard focus order (chart → legend → badges → tooltip), SR text templates for badges and axis states

Maya (Design): final microcopy choices: - badge: "5 bursts > 10k r/s" (hover: counts by sustained/single) - axis: "Throughput (requests/s)" - subtitle: "Unit: auto • Smoothing: off" - log mode label: "Log scale" with tooltip explaining usage

Priya (Product): sounds good. can we also add a tiny help link in the chart header "How to read this chart" which opens a short modal explaining units, smoothing, and spikes?

Maya (Design): yes will add that in the mock. thanks all — I'll push an updated Figma with the inset variant and badge icons tomorrow :raised_hands:

deploy-bot: Maya updated file "throughput-v2" (v6)

Noah (Eng): follow-up: prefer to surface the spike summary in the API as a compact array so third parties can surface the same badges in their UIs

Maya (Design): noted. Will add a note in the spec doc about the spike API shape and the subtitle requirement

Ravi (Accessibility): I'll test the mock once it's up and send any a11y fixes earlier rather than later

Priya (Product): thanks team — will queue this for next sprint refinement
